parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented targeting of gender-nonconforming people by police, border officers or the public, and no traveler-facing restriction on documents, facilities or care is documented. The documented negative material concerns sexual orientation: hate-crime enforcement failures (2020 attack, downgraded prosecution; second city's closed investigation) — but courts and the national prosecution service produced recourse, and prosecutions were reopened, showing institutions acting at least reactively. Societal conservatism (clerical hostility, large counter-Pride crowds) is hostility toward a Pride event, not toward trans visitors, and sits at friction-to-hostility for a traveller. No gender-identity anti-discrimination provision and no nonbinary recognition are resident-facing gaps. Open questions (border screening, facilities, police treatment of trans people) are unanswered questions, not exposures. Extrapolating structural signals — decriminalised, rule-of-law state with functioning though imperfect hate-crime recourse, no documented trans-specific harm — resolves to Reduced Risk, below jurisdictions with documented trans-specific protections or acceptance traditions.

entry_documents.protection: Foreign passports govern; no document or marker mismatch practice recorded.
entry_documents.interaction: Residency-status coupling for a trans immigrant (recognition invalidating residency) is resident-specific, not visitor-facing.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented for trans people; no custody placement, detention or medical-verification practice recorded.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; no refusal of care or medication seizure recorded.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Cleric framing homosexuality as 'corruption' and 'unnatural prostitution', counter-Pride crowds of thousands; anti-LGBTI hate crime under-investigated (downgraded charge, lenient fine).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Regional human-rights court unanimous violations finding; national prosecution service reopened both cases.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing targets sexual orientation/Pride, not gender expression; enforcement gap partially remedied judicially.

minors_guardians.exposure: Adoption bar on foreign same-sex couples reaches a trans visitor whose relationship reads as same-sex; no other minor-specific exposure documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling parent faces this only in an adoption/residency scenario, not ordinary travel.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented homophobic attacks (capital, second city); sparse rural population with no queer scene outside the capital; police closed one investigation.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Prosecution service ordered reopening; Pride marches held with thousands participating.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Whether reopened cases yield outcomes is unresolved; city-to-city variation beyond two cases is expectation only.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity anti-discrimination provision; nonbinary identity unrecognised; hate-crime enforcement the main documented gap.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working courts (asylum overturn, rights ruling, reopenings) show recourse institutions respond; partnership law in force 2024 signals improving climate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Border screening, facilities access and police treatment of trans people remain open questions, not exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor features a universal, enforced visitor register with no remedy. This dossier documents no traveler-facing regime at all; its worst documented feature is an under-investigated hate-crime case with successful judicial recourse — materially lower risk.

That anchor documents discretionary border screening actually routing trans visitors to secondary inspection. Here border practice is an open question, not a documented exposure, so this jurisdiction sits slightly above it; both share administrative-not-criminal severity.

That anchor has an equality statute, police review board and protective enforcement. This jurisdiction lacks gender-identity protections and shows a hate-crime enforcement gap, but similar street-violence tier and working courts; it sits a step below, around 0.66.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime shows no traveler-facing trans-specific restriction at any stage: no criminalisation of gender expression, no documented facility, custody, border or care exposure. The documented hostility targets sexual orientation and Pride, and its principal harm — failed hate-crime investigation — was corrected through courts and prosecutor reopenings, evidencing functioning recourse rather than impunity. Societal conservatism, ranked 24th of 27 regionally, weights the visitor toward friction and misgendering rather than organised targeting. Missing data (trans-specific police treatment, screening, facilities) is extrapolated from structural signals: rule-of-law, decriminalised, no documented trans harm. An adult travelling alone faces low severity if outed; the travelling-with-minor adult meets only the foreign same-sex adoption bar in hypothetical adoption scenarios. Score 0.66.
